heading: Training changes can improve weak-to-strong generalization over naive fine-tuning
definition: a training change (auxiliary confidence loss, ensembling weak supervisors, loss variants) raises PGR over naive fine-tuning.
summary: Independent groups find that the auxiliary confidence loss, which encourages students to trust their own confident predictions over weak labels, helps, has no effect, or hurts depending on the task and model pair. Combining models' predictions (ensembling) and alternative losses also show gains, but most of these methods have been tested only by the researchers who proposed them.

suggested_status.by_scale: toy: R0 for the bold-section DPO-versus-SFT comparison, which reports performance rather than PGR (arXiv:2507.06187#r7, arXiv:2507.06187#r9). <1B: ? for reverse KL on GPT-2. arXiv:2502.11107 reports reverse KL beating KL in 12/12 GPT-2 settings and reverse CE matching or beating CE in 10/12, ties included. With Pythia, reverse losses beat forward losses in only 7/12 settings (arXiv:2502.11107#R1, arXiv:2502.11107#R2, arXiv:2502.11107#R4). arXiv:2506.03109 says in its text that reverse KL is 'more likely' to beat CE on clean GPT-2 data (arXiv:2506.03109#AG1). Its authors are not in the checked lists: R1 if it shares authors with arXiv:2502.11107, R2 if not. ? for the confidence loss: arXiv:2502.11107 says in its text that it modestly beats plain CE with GPT-2 on CAI-Harmless (Figure 3; no row), and in arXiv:2501.00418, with a Pythia-410M student, it ties naive on OOD robustness but beats it on adversarial robustness (arXiv:2501.00418#R15, arXiv:2501.00418#R16, arXiv:2501.00418#R25). C for boosting weak GPT-2 supervisors on SciQ (GPT-2 students up to GPT2-XL, 1.5B): AdaBoost and Gradient Boost students fall at or below the pre-boosting students in 5 of 6 cases (arXiv:2402.00667#T2-4, arXiv:2402.00667#T2-5, arXiv:2402.00667#T2-6, arXiv:2402.00667#T2-7, arXiv:2402.00667#T2-8, arXiv:2402.00667#T2-9), while EnsemW2S's binary AdaBoost reports average SciQ gains (arXiv:2505.21959#F5). Author overlap between these two studies is not recorded (counts: versions.V2.studies_by_size['<1B'] = 2). 1-10B: C for the auxiliary confidence loss on NLP tasks, where groups other than the original's disagree. With Llama3 8B supervised by Qwen1.5 0.5B, the auxiliary log-confidence loss beats cross-entropy on 16/21 datasets, but the paired t-test gives p=.135 and the Wilcoxon test p=.079 (web:https://blog.eleuther.ai/weak-to-strong#R3). Qwen-7B on SciQ gains with GPT2-Large, OPT-1.3B, Pythia-1.4B and BLOOM-1B1 supervisors; as PGR fractions, for example, 0.503→0.614 and 0.541→0.714. With GPT2-Large on CosmosQA the gain is absent (0.073 vs 0.077). On Llama-2-7B SLURP slot filling the PGR fraction falls 0.303→0.150 (arXiv:2406.03199#S2, arXiv:2406.03199#S4, arXiv:2406.03199#S6, arXiv:2406.03199#S8, arXiv:2406.03199#C1, arXiv:2406.03199#G2). On Amazon-WILDS, Conf's reported PGR is below naive, e.g. OOD Llama-3.1-8B 10.88→0.50 and in-domain Qwen-7B 52.59→27.37 (arXiv:2510.21332, text, Table 2; no rows). R0 for each proposer's own ensembling method: RAVEN with Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-7B (arXiv:2510.21332#r31, arXiv:2510.21332#r32), EnsemW2S with Qwen2.5-7B (arXiv:2505.21959#Q1), and Bayesian Multi-Weak with the auxiliary loss on Qwen-7B (arXiv:2406.03199#S22). R0 for debate-based oversight labels, which give no gain in their one study: in arXiv:2402.00667 (qwen-1.8b-chat teacher, qwen-7b-base student), accuracy is 0.819/0.822 vs 0.826 before oversight (arXiv:2402.00667#T5-1, arXiv:2402.00667#T5-2). This recipe differs from the debate ensembles at 10-100B (counts: versions.V2.studies_by_size['1-10B'] = 17). 10-100B: C for the auxiliary confidence loss on NLP classification. The tests with rows at this size are arXiv:2501.13124 and arXiv:2511.14166, which share all three authors and so count as one group. With Qwen-14B students, results depend on task and supervisor (PGR in %). From Qwen-7B: 41.2 vs naive 44.1 on SciQ, 17.4 vs 30.4 on CosmosQA, and 56.4 vs 51.3 on BoolQ (arXiv:2501.13124#R2, arXiv:2501.13124#R10, arXiv:2501.13124#R6). From GPT-2: 60.98 vs 45.99 on SciQ but −10.76 vs 3.92 on BoolQ (arXiv:2511.14166#T2-SciQ-GPT2-aux, arXiv:2511.14166#T2-BoolQ-GPT2-aux). arXiv:2501.13124 notes that its 7B→14B gap is small. R0 for RAVEN, whose gains at this size are partial: reported PGR 49.70→53.60 with Qwen2.5-14B and 17.50→19.00 with Meditron-70B (arXiv:2510.21332#r33, arXiv:2510.21332#r35). R0 for debate ensembles with Qwen-14B (arXiv:2501.13124#R4, arXiv:2501.13124#R8, arXiv:2501.13124#R12, arXiv:2501.13124#R16). ? for reverse losses. The Qwen2.5 gains are small-positive limits_scope evidence (arXiv:2502.11107#R7, arXiv:2502.11107#R8, arXiv:2502.11107#R10, arXiv:2502.11107#R11). A reverse-KL row from a group with a different author list is also a small positive change: Qwen-14B BoolQ/GPT-2 PGR 3.92%→5.52% (arXiv:2511.14166#T2-BoolQ-GPT2-rkl). That study's other reverse-KL rows are not shown in the pack (counts: versions.V2.studies_by_size['10-100B'] = 9). >100B: R0 for the gpt-oss-120b SFT+RL elicitation improvement with Llama3.1-8B supervision; C for adding RL with GPT-4o-mini supervision. Neither condition reports numerical PGR (arXiv:2604.22082#R4, arXiv:2604.22082#R5, arXiv:2604.22082#R6, arXiv:2604.22082#R16, arXiv:2604.22082#R17, arXiv:2604.22082#R18; arXiv:2604.22082#R1, arXiv:2604.22082#R2, arXiv:2604.22082#R3, arXiv:2604.22082#R10, arXiv:2604.22082#R11, arXiv:2604.22082#R12; counts: versions.V2.studies_by_size['>100B'] = 1). Size not disclosed (the original's GPT-4-family students): R0 for the confidence-loss gain at the original's scale and gap, which no other study in these records tests (arXiv:2312.09390#r6). arXiv:2409.07335#R6 repeats the original's numbers.
suggested_status.reason: C is suggested because the original's headline method is contested by groups that share no author with the original. The earlier R2 labels each rested on one study's own method. Baseline: the original reports that the auxiliary confidence loss raises median PGR from about 25% to nearly 80% for its smallest supervisor and largest student. It is slightly worse for smaller students and sometimes does not help much with small gaps (arXiv:2312.09390#r6, arXiv:2312.09390#r7, arXiv:2312.09390#r8). Method by method: (1) Confidence loss: C. Groups testing it on NLP tasks are EleutherAI; Cui et al. (arXiv:2406.03199); Lang, Huang and Li (arXiv:2501.13124 and arXiv:2511.14166, one group); and Jeon et al. (arXiv:2510.21332). Gains reproduce in some task and supervisor conditions and are absent or reversed in others (see by_scale). arXiv:2505.24313 reports in its text that AUX is below CE on some pairs. None of these tests reaches the original's scale and gap. Outside NLP classification the results are also mixed. Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct generation: average PGR 58.94% vs a checker-calculated 37.04% for naive W2S (arXiv:2605.27591#r1). Federated LLaMA-2 servers show small accuracy gains (arXiv:2607.29071#R2). With a Pythia-410M student, Aux-Loss ties naive on OOD robustness (75% vs 75%) but beats it on adversarial robustness (arXiv:2501.00418#R15, arXiv:2501.00418#R16, arXiv:2501.00418#R25). With CLIP linear probing, AuxConf+LP is far below CE+LP on Infograph (18.37 vs 30.55) and Quickdraw (30.59 vs 45.59) but 0.4–2 points above it on the other four DomainNet domains (arXiv:2511.18396#t1-aux-lp-infograph, arXiv:2511.18396#t1-aux-lp-quickdraw, arXiv:2511.18396#t1-aux-lp-clipart, arXiv:2511.18396#t1-aux-lp-sketch). Generative alignment and reward modelling show losses against their comparators (arXiv:2510.07884#r7, arXiv:2605.25629#R34). (2) Ensembling and boosting: R0 per method. The original did not test ensembling. RAVEN, EnsemW2S, co-supervision and Bayesian Multi-Weak gains all come from the methods' own authors (arXiv:2510.21332#r32, arXiv:2505.21959#Q1, arXiv:2402.15505#r15, arXiv:2406.03199#S22). Generic recipes give little or no gain. Safety voting goes 0.181→0.174 PGR as a fraction (arXiv:2410.12621#R8). Naive and FlyingSquid aggregation fall below the best single supervisor (arXiv:2406.03199#S12, arXiv:2406.03199#S14). Bootstrap bagging raises GPT-2 SciQ student accuracy in some pairs (0.659→0.678, 0.676→0.688) but not with GPT2-XL (0.682 unchanged), with no PGR reported (arXiv:2402.00667#T1-6, arXiv:2402.00667#T1-7, arXiv:2402.00667#T1-8). Boosting is C (see <1B). (3) Debate: R0 per recipe. Debate ensembles gain in their proposers' study (see 10-100B). Debate RL training beats RLAIF in its proposers' study (arXiv:2608.17776#r3). Another study's debate-based oversight labels give no gain (see 1-10B). (4) Reverse KL/CE: ? at <1B (pending arXiv:2506.03109's authors) and ? at 10-100B (see by_scale). arXiv:2505.24313 reports in its text that reverse CE alone is below CE on Qwen pairs, 94.93 vs 96.03. (5) Bootstrapping: R0. Only the original reports the chess gain, with small NLP gains and none for reward modelling (arXiv:2312.09390#r9, arXiv:2312.09390#r10, arXiv:2312.09390#r11). arXiv:2409.07335 repeats the original's numbers. The independent numerical test uses Qwen2.5 3B–14B on-policy distillation chains, a different recipe, and every chain peaks below direct transfer (arXiv:2609.32722#bootstrap-vanilla-3b, arXiv:2609.32722#bootstrap-vanilla-14b): C in that recipe. Two other groups report bootstrapping without numerical PGR: arXiv:2406.11431 says in its text that it can improve Mistral-7B accuracy in a harmlessness/SimPO setting (Figure 9(b); no row), and arXiv:2405.16236 reports partial protection against degradation on a GPT-4o-mini persona task, with no naive baseline in Table 1 (arXiv:2405.16236#tb17). (6) The other methods (filtering, selection, BIRD, CACE and most on-policy-distillation variants): R0 each, tested only by their proposers (support items). Three lines involve more than one study, with author overlap not recorded. Direct-OPD gains in arXiv:2607.05394 (AIME 2024 56.7→63.1; arXiv:2607.05394#r05, arXiv:2607.05394#r11) but averages 37.81 vs OPD 45.67 in arXiv:2609.08798 (arXiv:2609.08798#r39): ?. W2S-OPD beats OPD in arXiv:2607.26246 (+3.1 to +7.8 on math; arXiv:2607.26246#r1) and in arXiv:2609.08798 (49.22 vs 45.67; arXiv:2609.08798#r40): ?. Preference optimization beats SFT on the same weak data in arXiv:2507.06187 (arXiv:2507.06187#r1, arXiv:2507.06187#r2) and arXiv:2606.00357 (arXiv:2606.00357#r24, arXiv:2606.00357#r43). DPO applied after weak-label SFT gives no gain or declines in arXiv:2501.07886 (text, Figure 4 and Table 3; no row) and arXiv:2407.13647 (text, no row). The recipes differ: ?. One possible cross-group match is adaptive confidence distillation. It was proposed in arXiv:2402.03749 (CIFAR-100 ResNet32×4 accuracy: KD 77.92, AdaptConf 78.48; arXiv:2402.03749#r1, arXiv:2402.03749#r5). It also beats CE in every DomainNet domain in arXiv:2511.18396 (Infograph 33.78% vs 30.55%, arXiv:2511.18396#t1-adapt-lp-infograph). Author overlap between these two studies is not in the checked lists. Script coverage: versions.V2.studies_tested = 52, versions.V2.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original = 0, and versions.V2.tested_with_uncertainty = 23. The checked author lists agree for arXiv:2406.03199, arXiv:2501.13124, arXiv:2502.11107, arXiv:2510.21332, arXiv:2511.14166 and EleutherAI (authors not recorded, marked no overlap): none shares an author with the original. Preference-training and elicitation comparisons supply additional behavioural evidence, without reported numerical PGR (arXiv:2507.06187#r1, arXiv:2507.06187#r2, arXiv:2507.06187#r3, arXiv:2507.06187#r4; arXiv:2604.22082#R16, arXiv:2604.22082#R17, arXiv:2604.22082#R18). The script's verdict totals have not been recomputed after checker corrections and are not corrected-label counts.
suggested_status.open_questions: Would a matched-data, matched-tuning reproduction of auxiliary confidence loss with students of 70B or more recover PGR over seeds? Would method gains survive validation-based threshold selection? Can the same method raise PGR across tasks and supervisor–student pairs outside its authors' settings? Does bootstrapping improve PGR consistently on open-model NLP classification? Can the above-100B elicitation result be reproduced independently with numerical PGR and both supervisor conditions? What makes the confidence-loss gain depend on task and supervisor at 7–14B, for example SciQ/GPT-2 gains vs BoolQ/GPT-2 losses with the same Qwen-14B student? Would a significant aggregate gain on EleutherAI's 21 datasets move the confidence loss from C to R2? Do arXiv:2506.03109 and arXiv:2505.24313 share authors with arXiv:2502.11107, and does arXiv:2511.18396 share authors with arXiv:2402.03749? Distinct authors would make GPT-2 reverse KL and adaptive confidence distillation candidates for R2. Would arXiv:2511.14166's other reverse-KL rows settle the ? for reverse losses at 10-100B?

source.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization
source.authors: Collin Burns; Pavel Izmailov; J. Kirchner; Bowen Baker; Leo Gao; Leopold Aschenbrenner; Yining Chen; Adrien Ecoffet; Manas R. Joglekar; Jan Leike; I. Sutskever; Jeff Wu

original_result.setup: The original study added an auxiliary confidence loss, which encourages students to trust their own confident predictions over weak labels, when fine-tuning GPT-4-family students on weak labels.
original_result.result: For the smallest supervisor and largest student, adding the loss raised median performance gap recovery across 22 NLP datasets from about 25% to nearly 80%. The loss performed slightly worse for smaller students and sometimes offered little benefit or degraded performance when supervisor and student were close in size.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: Segment, Select, Correct outperformed longer training across all tested splits for segmenting objects described in text.
Specialized weak supervisors and denoising raised gap recovered on ImageNet and DomainNet.
Auxiliary loss, Bayesian supervision, and token probability estimation increased gap recovered in tested tasks.
Confidence loss, generative fine-tuning, and bootstrapping improved gap recovered in the domains tested.
Weak-supervisor ensembles improved student performance and gap recovered across tested Qwen and Pythia settings.
Filtering uncertain labels and reweighting by reliability increased gap recovered in most settings using all data.
Bootstrap bagging and interaction-based oversight improved student accuracy in selected GPT2 pairings.
MACPO with three weak teachers outperformed naive fine-tuning across alignment datasets and judgments.
Intermediate-model bootstrapping improved Mistral-7B generalization under implicit conflict.
Consistency-filtered Weak-ICL fine-tuning increased gap recovered across all tested math comparisons.
Adaptive confidence loss outperformed naive distillation across all tested vision pairs using only teacher supervision.
Retraining on confidence-selected subsets improved average and minimum group accuracy in most tested vision settings.
Debate ensembles increased gap recovered over naive fine-tuning across all four tasks.
Filtering for correct reasoning traces improved both tested Qwen students across every comparison.
Adaptive confidence loss and CPL improved classification over cross-entropy across DomainNet domains.
Iterative label refinement with comparison feedback improved all four weakly supervised settings.
Refining labels with in-context learning improved weakly supervised training and avoided declines in content scores.
Confidence filtering and filtered relabeling substantially increased math gap recovered at selected thresholds.
In GPT-2 KL comparisons, reverse-direction losses consistently improved clean-label training; Qwen gains were modest.
Preference tuning favoring weak-model over weaker-model outputs outperformed supervised training on the weak model’s chosen outputs.
Selective supervision with graph smoothing increased gap recovered across all tested task–supervisor pairs.
CACE, teacher ensembles, and reverse cross-entropy improved performance under their tested conditions.
Curated biological-reasoning subsets outperformed full-set training when transferring to KEGG.
Debate training improved peak accuracy and stability, with extra rebuttals helping weaker judges.
Adaptive weak-supervisor ensembling increased gap recovered across image, text, and preference tasks.
BIRD increased SciQ gap recovered for both tested students.
Alice improved over Q-CoT-A in most tested pair–task settings.
The α = 0.5 setting improved average accuracy across tested federated language-model settings.
Confidence loss increased average gap recovered in single-client and five-client training.
Successive training additions improved out-of-distribution video-quality assessment across tested student backbones.
Preference training and selected LoRA merging methods improved over their respective baselines.
Alternative divergence losses improved reward modeling over cross-entropy under some noise conditions.
P-OPD distillation outperformed matched on-policy distillation (OPD) across tested proxy pairings.
Adding reinforcement learning after supervised training better drew out capabilities with a very weak supervisor.
Waypoint-OPD improved domain averages over direct on-policy distillation (Direct-OPD) across all tested students.
Direct-OPD (direct on-policy distillation) outperformed standard on-policy distillation for R1-Distill-7B on AIME 2024.
W2S-OPD distillation improved math performance over direct on-policy distillation.
ANCHOR improved source generalization over naive training.
Re-anchoring the weak policy shift improved average performance over plain OPD.
ConG outperformed weak supervised fine-tuning across model and human judges.
Tree-structured preference training improved Llama3-8B performance on AlfWorld.
Delta-OPD usually improved peak gains.
Trust filtering outperformed naive weak supervision across every tested pair of differently sized models.
Confidence-weighted preference losses improved recovery for small and mid-sized students.
Confidence weighting helped only with the fewest gold-standard labels; distillation gave no gain.
Persona-training changes left substantial corruption, while the auxiliary-loss proxy traded style for content.
Ensembling without auxiliary loss did not beat naive training; gains from other methods were small.
Bootstrapping produced limited improvements on natural-language processing and reward modeling.
Ensembling lowered ARC gap recovered and provided little benefit for some small Pythia pairs.
Auxiliary confidence loss improved adversarial accuracy but matched naive training’s out-of-distribution accuracy.
Reliability-based training failed for selected model pairs and weakened when training data were matched.
Some bagging variants produced negligible gains or left student accuracy unchanged.
MACPO gains depended on teacher number and iteration, with single-teacher training eventually degrading.
Direct preference optimization (DPO) in a second stage reduced MATH accuracy across all three supervisors.
Vision distillation gains were sometimes tiny; several alternative losses underperformed knowledge distillation (KD).
Retraining on confidence-selected subsets reduced performance for some BFFHQ and BG-COCO model pairs.
Confidence losses gave small gains, while alternative contexts often failed without debate ensembles.
Correct-trace filtering gave mixed results for Qwen2.5-32B with the 14B(R) teacher.
Auxiliary confidence loss produced small classification gains in some DomainNet domains.
Preference-loss variants gave little improvement; naive relabeling worsened performance on every tested task.
Filtering gains were smaller on SciQ and could reverse with unsuitable thresholds.
Reverse-direction losses improved inconsistently on Pythia and often underperformed with heavily corrupted labels.
Preferring Llama-3.1-8B outputs over its smaller sibling yielded only a small average gain.
Alternative losses and graph smoothing gave negligible or negative gains in some settings.
CACE gains were sometimes negligible, while RCE and auxiliary loss could underperform cross-entropy.
Copy-paste augmentation increased coverage but failed to improve segmentation quality.
Biological-reasoning curation gave small PerturbQA gains but reduced RBIO1 transfer performance.
Alternative AI-feedback reinforcement learning and debate variants failed to improve performance or enabled reward hacking.
RAVEN delivered only small or negligible gains in gap recovered in some scaling settings.
BIRD produced only a modest gain for GPT2-Large on Cosmos QA.
Alice improved HotpotQA by less than one point in the selected model pairings.
Federated training gains were small on average and reversed on some non-IID benchmarks.
Confidence loss lowered five-client CommonsenseQA gap recovered but improved single-client AQuA-RAT performance from negative values.
In-domain video-quality gains were small, and confidence loss added no benefit.
Sequential training, joint training, and reasoning averaging underperformed the best single set of weight changes.
No alternative divergence loss consistently outperformed cross-entropy across datasets and model pairs.
P-OPD performance collapsed when its calibration set was too small for the proxy model.
Adding reinforcement learning had mixed effects on drawing out capabilities with GPT-4o-mini supervision.
Waypoint-OPD distillation gains reversed on two math benchmarks and were negligible on another.
W2S-OPD distillation gains on code were small and depended on the amplification strength.
Confidence loss and weight interpolation did not consistently improve reward models under preference shift.
Auxiliary log-confidence loss improved most datasets, but the overall gains were not statistically clear.
Auxiliary confidence loss gave small generative alignment gains but remained below the strong base model.
TreeDPO preference-training gains weakened or reversed with unfavorable hyperparameters and excessive trajectory sampling.
Delta-OPD gains shrank with teacher scale, and some transfer pairs lacked a slope advantage.
NTF sometimes delivered small gains, while ensemble agreement selection underperformed naive training.
CW-DPO preference training gains diminished for large students and did not consistently outperform online WS-DPO.
Generalized cross-entropy and Co-teaching underperformed hard-label binary cross-entropy with few gold labels on ISIC 2019.
Auxiliary loss reduced SLURP gap recovered; the five-model Joint Decoding method collapsed.
Boosting usually failed to improve students, and debate oversight reduced student performance.
Adapted confidence loss generally underperformed naive supervised fine-tuning (SFT), with a small HH-Harmless gain.
Bootstrapping weak supervisors with voting slightly reduced gap recovered on safety tasks.
Original confidence losses matched or underperformed naive training across tested 7B–14B tasks.
Auxiliary confidence loss substantially reduced performance when fitting linear classifiers to frozen Infograph and Quickdraw representations.
Loss variants reduced gap recovered below naive training, making it negative on BoolQ-GPT2.
Auxiliary confidence loss reduced gap recovered on Amazon-WILDS and FMoW.
BIRD reduced gap recovered on CosmosQA and left it at zero on BoolQ.
Alice underperformed original weak-to-strong Q-CoT-A on HotpotQA with Llama 3.2 1B→3B.
SEAM pushed in-distribution performance below the weak teacher despite out-of-distribution gains.
Alternative losses, strong-to-strong relabeling, and probe methods failed to consistently improve vanilla training.
Direct-OPD averaged below the plain OPD baseline across three tasks transferring from 4B-parameter to 8B-parameter models.
Training through intermediate-sized models underperformed training the target directly with the 0.5B-parameter expert model’s supervision.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: The auxiliary confidence loss at the original's scale and gap: GPT-4-family-sized students with the largest supervisor-student gaps, where the original reports a median PGR of about 25%→80%. Independent confidence-loss tests use open students up to 70B, mostly 7–14B, including FedSLM's LLaMA-2-7B/13B servers.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V2.studies_by_size['>100B'] = 1, and that student is gpt-oss-120b in arXiv:2604.22082, which tests SFT+RL, not the confidence loss. EleutherAI's untested-parts line names larger scales, where Burns et al. find log-confidence more effective. arXiv:2501.13124's problems line notes its gap is only 7B vs 14B.

untested.what: Burns-style bootstrapping through intermediate sizes on NLP classification, measured by PGR with open models. The bootstrapping tests that exist are on-policy distillation chains for math (arXiv:2609.32722), a persona task with no naive baseline (arXiv:2405.16236), a harmlessness text claim (arXiv:2406.11431), and a paper that repeats the original's numbers (arXiv:2409.07335).
untested.basis: Untested-parts lines of arXiv:2511.14166, arXiv:2605.25629, arXiv:2505.23933, arXiv:2402.15505, 173d42ed4cd2dd8e988e628b97727a6c6f52f7a2 and arXiv:2607.11505 name bootstrapping as untested.

wording_issues.issue: PGR values require attention to the reference and normalization. Reward-model PGR reaches 1537.5% with a ceiling of 88.05, and −1315.4% for SEAM (arXiv:2605.25629). On ETHICS-cm, filtering Llama2-7B labels for Llama2-13B improves fractional PGR −2.250→−0.476; this is a method gain despite remaining below the supervisor (arXiv:2406.19032). Safety voting lowers GPT-2-medium fractional PGR 0.181→0.174; statistical significance is not established (arXiv:2410.12621). EnsemW2S raises ARC accuracy by 1.28 points while fractional PGR decreases approximately 0.292→0.168 when each student is normalized against its own supervisor (arXiv:2505.21959).

Several method studies report no PGR. FedSLM reports nine-benchmark accuracy (%), e.g. LLaMA-2-7B IID 69.9→71.0 (arXiv:2607.29071). Waypoint-OPD reports mean@32 or mean@8 accuracy (%) (arXiv:2610.21601). P-OPD reports Mean@k scores. Its one PGR, about 0.58 (a fraction) for the Qwen3-1.7B proxy → Qwen3-8B target, was computed by the verdict model against a 44.5 ceiling (arXiv:2607.11505). arXiv:2402.00667 reports accuracy with no true-label ceiling, so no PGR. The also list holds other studies whose untested-parts or problems lines say PGR is not computed.

Comparators vary. Preference-delta merging uses the best single preference delta (arXiv:2606.00357). ConG reports comparisons with a strong base and Weak SFT before or after alignment; the strong-base comparison does not itself test improvement over weak-label fine-tuning (arXiv:2510.07884). The segmentation '+40 epochs' arm continues cross-entropy training of bootstrapped LAVT on fixed weak pseudo-label masks, so it qualifies as continued weak-label training (arXiv:2310.13479). FedSLM's α=0 arm uses cross-entropy against weak-model soft labels without auxiliary confidence loss; both arms use federated aggregation, so this is a weak-label fine-tuning comparator (arXiv:2607.29071).

The term covers different implementations. The generation baseline pools teacher and student outputs and is not Burns' original objective (arXiv:2410.07672). A data-doubling proxy is used because GPT weights were inaccessible (arXiv:2405.16236). EleutherAI presents its α=0.5 log-confidence objective as the simplest form of Burns' loss; its description does not establish a different loss. With CLIP and linear probing on DomainNet Infograph, AuxConf accuracy is 18.37%, AdaptConf 33.78%, and CE 30.55%: the auxiliary and adaptive objectives have opposite directions relative to CE in this setting (arXiv:2511.18396).

Method gains depend on condition and metric. With Qwen-14B and a GPT-2 supervisor, auxiliary-loss PGR (%) rises 45.99→60.98 on SciQ but falls 3.92→−10.76 on BoolQ (arXiv:2511.14166). Auxiliary loss raises SciQ PGR but lowers fractional SLURP PGR 0.303→0.150 for Llama-2-7B supervised by GPT2-Large (arXiv:2406.03199). Correct-only filtering at Qwen2.5-32B is mixed: accuracy changes are +0.20 points on MATH, −0.74 on Minerva and −1.01 on GPQA (arXiv:2505.20072). Confidence-weighted preference optimization has condition-dependent offline gains; online HH-RLHF GRA falls 56.3→55.1 from WS-DPO to CW-DPO. That study does not report PGR (arXiv:2603.04968).

wording_issues.phrase: training change (auxiliary confidence loss, ensembling weak supervisors, loss variants)
wording_issues.issue: The examples do not specify data curation with in-context learning (arXiv:2407.13647) or LoRA merging of preference deltas and weight editing (arXiv:2606.00357). P-OPD transfers a proxy expert/base log-ratio with target/base regularization and calibration coefficient λ through a modified signal-transfer loss, so it fits 'loss variants' (arXiv:2607.11505). Waypoint-OPD uses gated, normalized transfer of an RL-induced policy shift (arXiv:2610.21601). counts: versions.V2.main_rows_by_operation lists weight_edit 7, scaling 8 and evaluation 9 next to training 415.

The phrase covers distinct procedures with different outcomes. Debate ensembles raise Qwen-14B SciQ PGR 44.1%→76.5% (arXiv:2501.13124). On SciQ, AdaBoost and Gradient Boost medium/XL students have absent or reversed accuracy gains, while Gradient Boost GPT2-large improves fractional accuracy 0.680→0.688 (arXiv:2402.00667). Safety voting lowers GPT-2-medium fractional PGR 0.181→0.174; statistical significance is not established (arXiv:2410.12621). Adaptive weighting with RAVEN raises Qwen2.5-7B Amazon-WILDS OOD reported PGR 30.35→85.88 (arXiv:2510.21332).

In P-OPD, only the Qwen3-1.7B proxy is clearly weak against the proposed Qwen3-8B reference. The Qwen3-4B supervisor scores 46.5 and Skywork-OR1-Math-7B scores 45.2, exceeding the proposed strong reference of 44.5. Their P-OPD accuracy improvements over OPD, 43.6→47.4 and 44.1→52.5 respectively, therefore do not establish improved positive-gap PGR (arXiv:2607.11505).

method_sensitivity.factor: Weak supervisor or proxy identity and strength
method_sensitivity.what: Qwen-14B on BoolQ: auxiliary loss lowers PGR 3.92%→−10.76% with GPT-2 but raises it 17.56%→32.85% with Qwen-1.8B. These are auxiliary-loss values, not product-loss values. gpt-oss-120b: RL after SFT raises elicitation from 0.40–0.75 to 0.88–0.99 with Llama3.1-8B; with GPT-4o-mini, SFT+RL gives 0.86/0.97/0.93 versus SFT 0.85/0.91/0.94, described as no improvement. Qwen-7B/CosmosQA, fractional PGR: auxiliary loss gives 0.162→0.399 with Pythia but 0.073 versus without-aux 0.077 ± 0.032 with GPT2-Large, an absent gain. Qwen3-8B math Mean@16, P-OPD versus OPD: 1.7B proxy 36.6 versus 28.3; 4B 47.4 versus 43.6; Skywork 52.5 versus 44.1. The latter two cannot establish positive-gap PGR gains: supervisors exceed the proposed strong reference. Code Mean@8 with the 4B proxy improves 59.2→60.5; its ceiling is missing.

Baseline: the original reports median PGR about 25% with naive fine-tuning versus nearly 80% with confidence loss for its smallest weak supervisor and largest strong student; confidence loss is slightly worse for smaller students. Correct-only filtering beats W2SR by 0.6–10 points at 7B and 14B, but gives +0.20/−0.74/−1.01 at 32B; the +0.20-point case is partial, 83.60%→83.80%, without established insignificance. CW-DPO versus WS-DPO is not uniformly beneficial below 14B: OPT-13B/UFB falls 63.4→63.1 GRA. Qwen2.5-14B DPO gives HH-RLHF 81.4→80.6, TL;DR 64.8→66.0 and UFB 78.3→80.1 GRA. These are GRA comparisons, not PGR; annotator training also differs. Bootstrap bagging leaves GPT2-XL accuracy unchanged at 0.682, an absent V2 gain.

Filtering threshold: Llama 3 70B MATH PGR is −12.77% at 100%; Deepseek 67B MATH is 7.32% at 90% versus naive 65.85%. Contrastive α works best at 0.3–0.5. W2S-OPD amplification α falls below OPD when small and declines when large. P-OPD calibration λ, Qwen3-8B target, eight-benchmark math Mean@16, Qwen3-4B proxy: λ=0→0, 0.5→30.85, 0.75→44.14, 0.95→44.46, 1.0→44.92, 1.1→45.17 (used to select λ), 1.5→38.74. The λ=0 collapse cannot establish reversed positive-gap PGR: no matched eight-benchmark OPD/PGR reference is supplied, and the 4B supervisor exceeds the four-benchmark strong reference. With the Qwen3-1.7B proxy, λ=0.5 gives zero, including on the four-benchmark subset with OPD 28.3 and a positive supervisor-to-reference gap; this reverses the method gain.

method_sensitivity.factor: Gold-label budget mixed with weak labels
method_sensitivity.what: ResNet-18 on ISIC 2019 with BiomedCLIP weak labels (5K), test AUC. At 500/1,000 gold labels, GCE improves hard-label BCE 0.597/0.624 to 0.660/0.731; Co-teaching improves those same references to 0.720/0.755. These are observed method gains. The hard-label arms alone cannot determine a V2 gain; gold-only AUC 0.812/0.854 is a separate reference, and remaining below it does not make the method gains incomplete. At 10–50 gold labels, GCE and Co-teaching are 0.02–0.04 AUC below hard-label BCE (text). Confidence-weighted BCE gives +0.02 (0.615) at 500 and +0.04 (0.664) at 1,000.

On clean labels, reverse KL beats KL in 12/12 GPT-2 settings; with 50% swapped labels, RKL is worse in 2 of 3 settings, e.g. 45.375 vs 53.950 (arXiv:2502.11107). Hellinger beats CE at noise 0.1–0.4, while at 50% noise χ2/JS gain up to about 8.6 points and Hellinger falls below CE on CAI-Harmless (arXiv:2506.03109). RCE keeps high accuracy under smoothed teacher labels (α=0.001) while CE drops, yet falls below CE under ordinary labels (arXiv:2505.24313).

In LLaVA video quality assessment, cumulative additions raise OOD SRCC 0.591→0.745. In-domain SRCC at stages I–VI is 0.849, 0.856, 0.858, 0.857, 0.860, 0.865; the confidence-loss step decreases it by 0.001. For Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct SEAM reward models trained on HelpSteer3, transfer to Anthropic Helpful gives OOD AOG 9.95 versus naive 1.46, while source in-distribution WRG is −15.67 versus naive 1.71. AOG and WRG are distinct metrics. With Pythia, auxiliary loss and naive training both reach 75% OOD robustness accuracy in Weak TFT, an absent V2 gain; auxiliary loss exceeds naive on adversarial accuracy in Weak+WTS TFT.

method_sensitivity.factor: Matching of data size and tuning between method and baseline
method_sensitivity.what: Full-data reliability methods use more examples than naive. With size matched, re-weighting reverses the method gain: fractional PGR −0.618 versus naive 0.205 on Hellaswag/Llama2-13B and −0.234 versus 0.239 on GSM8K/Llama2-13B (text; no extracted sampled-result rows). CACE is the best of 4 η settings against untuned CE: Qwen-14B/CAI-Harmless 96.03%→96.08%; another reported pair 66.15%→66.18%. These are small positive, partial gains; statistical significance is not reported. For arXiv:2503.04249, headline results are maxima over threshold sweeps evaluated on evaluation/test sets; a separate selection procedure is not described. For arXiv:2407.13647, test accuracies of three variants and the best weak-ICL result are reported; test-based variant selection is an inference, and the selection protocol is unstated.

method_sensitivity.factor: Seed variance, run count and reported uncertainty
method_sensitivity.what: BIRD's Cosmos QA drop (47.00%→42.76% PGR) is within a soft-label seed spread of 16.94–95.15 (arXiv:2505.23933). SLURP estimates vary widely, e.g. aux PGR −0.250 ± 0.224 (arXiv:2406.03199). On-policy distillation uses one run per configuration (arXiv:2609.32722). CACE's study reports at least three independent random seeds for all experiments; Table 1 gives best outcomes over loss-specific hyperparameters without error bars or an explicit seed-aggregation rule (arXiv:2505.24313).

method_sensitivity.factor: Aggregation level, data partition and training step
method_sensitivity.what: Waypoint-OPD gains on every domain average (e.g. Qwen3-8B math 53.96→56.14) but is reversed on single HMMT benchmarks for Qwen3-14B (47.60→47.08) and Qwen3-30B-A3B (33.05→32.77). For Qwen3-8B on HMMT November 2025 at step 100, the gain is 0.10 points (arXiv:2610.21601). FedSLM α=0.5 vs α=0, average accuracy (%): LLaMA-2-7B IID 69.9→71.0 and non-IID 67.8→68.2; LLaMA-2-13B IID 70.6→71.4 and non-IID 67.4→68.1. 7B HellaSwag rises 75.1→80.2 under IID but falls 76.6→76.0 under non-IID, per the verdict's reading of Table II (arXiv:2607.29071).

method_sensitivity.factor: Method components (Waypoint-OPD prefix gate and batch-scale normalization)
method_sensitivity.what: On the Qwen3-8B math average (mean@32, seven benchmarks), full Waypoint-OPD scores 56.14. Removing the gate gives 53.50, lower on all seven benchmarks per the verdict. Fixing the batch-scale multiplier (no normalization) gives 55.22, which is still above Direct-OPD at 53.96 (arXiv:2610.21601).

status_amendment.public_note: We now rate this claim method by method. The original's main method, an extra confidence loss, helps in some independent tests but not in others, so the overall level drops from "independently reproduced" to "contested", and most other methods have only been tested by the teams that proposed them.
status_amendment.level_changed_because: R2 was based on three single-study results, each the authors' own method: reverse KL in arXiv:2502.11107 at <1B, and RAVEN in arXiv:2510.21332 at 1-10B and 10-100B (r33 is only partial). The README counts these as R0, not as a different group reproducing a result. Rebuilt method by method, the original's headline method, the auxiliary confidence loss, has been tested by groups that share no author with the original, and their results disagree. EleutherAI's 21-dataset gain is not significant (p=.135, p=.079). Gains appear in some task–supervisor pairs: SciQ with GPT-2, OPT, Pythia and BLOOM supervisors, and CosmosQA with Pythia and GPT-2 supervisors (arXiv:2406.03199, arXiv:2511.14166). The loss is absent or reversed in others: SciQ and CosmosQA with a Qwen-7B supervisor, CosmosQA with GPT2-Large, BoolQ with GPT-2, SLURP and Amazon-WILDS (arXiv:2501.13124, arXiv:2406.03199, arXiv:2511.14166, arXiv:2510.21332). That makes it contested (C). Most other methods are R0, tested only by their proposers. Boosting is C. Reverse losses, Direct-OPD, W2S-OPD, preference optimization and adaptive confidence distillation are ?: author overlap is unchecked for some of them, and the reverse-loss and preference-optimization lines also have hidden rows or differing recipes (see reason).
